# PureMac

> PureMac is a free, native, open-source Mac utility for cleanup, app management, storage exploration, duplicate detection, and system checks.

## Product
- Current stable GUI release verified 24 October 2026: 3.1.0.
- macOS 13 Ventura or later. Universal Apple Silicon and Intel binary.
- Developer ID signed, Apple-notarized. MIT license, no paid feature tier.
- Smart Care scans cleanup categories with progress, cancellation, filters, exclusions, and manual confirmation.
- Local AI Models lists Ollama models and Hugging Face downloads for manual review. It is excluded from Smart Scan and scheduled cleaning, and nothing is preselected.
- App Uninstaller discovers related files using heuristic matching. Users must review matches.
- Orphan Finder surfaces files associated with apps no longer installed.
- Space Explorer measures allocated folder storage and reports skipped or inaccessible items. A read-only treemap view draws the same sizes as proportional tiles (docs/SPACE-TREEMAP.md).
- Duplicate Finder verifies exact matches by content hash and protects one copy per group.
- Similar Photos reviews likely matches and reveals them in Finder. It does not delete photos.
- Protection checks Gatekeeper, FileVault, firewall, SIP, and XProtect metadata. It is not an antivirus scan.
- Performance shows process CPU and memory usage, startup items, and local snapshots.
- App Updates checks and upgrades Homebrew-managed casks. It does not cover all installed apps.
- AI Agent Data lists large, regenerable data of Claude Desktop, Codex, Antigravity, and Cursor for review only. Rows are never preselected, excluded from Smart Scan and scheduled cleaning, and moved to Trash only while the owning app is not running. Details: docs/AI-AGENT-DATA.md.
- Developer cleanup (Dev Tool Caches, Docker Cache, Git Worktrees, Local AI Models, AI Agent Data): map of categories, shared safety rules and debugging in docs/DEVELOPER-CLEANUP.md.
- Settings includes appearance, language, Full Disk Access, and user-requested GitHub release checks.

## Removal behavior
Move to Trash (recoverable until Trash is emptied): user-level app uninstalling, orphan removal, exact-duplicate removal, XcodeBuildMCP DerivedData, and AI Agent Data (only while the owning app is not running). Permanent (cannot be undone): dashboard/category cleanup of ordinary caches, scheduled auto-clean, Trash emptying, administrator-authorized removal, local snapshot deletion, CLI cleanup, and the developer categories, which go through the tool that owns the data where one exists. Docker Cache rows run `docker builder prune`, `docker container prune`, `docker image prune` or `docker volume rm <listed names>` (never `system prune` or `volume prune`); simulator runtimes use `simctl runtime delete`. Dev Tool Caches use `uv cache clean` and `go clean` for those two tools and delete the other cache folders (Gradle is skipped while it runs; Maven and NuGet are never auto-selected). Git Worktrees run `git worktree remove` without `--force`, `git worktree prune` for already-missing worktrees and optionally `git branch -d`, or delete only the git-ignored build folders (node_modules, .next, dist) of a worktree that stays. Local AI Models use the Ollama API (`ollama rm` if the API is unreachable), `hf cache rm`, or delete one validated folder. Docker Cache, Git Worktrees and Local AI Models are removed only from their own screen after each risk is confirmed, never from the Overview; Git Worktrees, Local AI Models and AI Agent Data are excluded from Smart Scan and scheduled cleaning, and no developer-category row holding user data is preselected. Manual removal requires confirmation. Scheduled auto-clean runs unattended once enabled. Keep backups and review selections. Purgeable space is managed by macOS and is not promised as recoverable cleanup. Details: docs/DEVELOPER-CLEANUP.md, docs/DOCKER.md, docs/GIT-WORKTREES.md, docs/DEV-TOOL-CACHES.md, docs/LOCAL-AI-MODELS.md, docs/AI-AGENT-DATA.md.

## Privacy
No telemetry, analytics, or crash reporting. Local scans and cleanup work offline. Scanned paths and file contents are not uploaded. GitHub release checks and Homebrew update operations use the network. Homebrew operations run with analytics disabled.

## Install
- GUI: `brew install --cask puremac`
- Signed DMG: https://github.com/momenbasel/PureMac/releases/latest
- CLI: `brew install momenbasel/tap/puremac-cli`
- If Homebrew requires tap trust: run `brew tap momenbasel/tap`, then `brew trust --tap momenbasel/tap`, then repeat the CLI install command.
- CLI cleanup is permanent; preview with `puremac clean dev --dry-run`.
